summary.headline: V-Mart Q4 FY26 revenue rose 24% with 12% LTL growth and EBITDA up 56% to INR106 crore at 10.9% margin.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was a strong quarter: 29 new stores opened (record quarterly additions), like-to-like growth of 12% (V-Mart 12%, Unlimited 9%), and total sales up 24%. EBITDA rose 56% YoY to INR106 crore with margin up 220 bps to 10.9%, and adjusted PAT reached INR10 crore. Full-year PAT grew 6x to INR124 crore (3.3% margin). Management flagged rising polyester/crude-linked raw material costs and yarn availability issues for FY27 deliveries, plus a 1% YoY gross margin decline in the quarter.

financial_highlights.change: Due to inventory provisioning and 12% fall in LimeRoad commission income
LimeRoad expense cut, lower ESOP expense, lower offline marketing
vs negative INR33 crore last year
Driven by festive mix, lower discounting, better full-price sell-through

segments.name: V-Mart (core)
segments.commentary: Like-to-like growth of 12% in Q4; management says footfalls growing and new stores are performing above network throughput in Tier 2 and Tier 3 towns.

segments.name: Unlimited (South)
segments.commentary: South Unlimited revenue grew 28% with EBITDA up 63%; management plans more South store openings. Sales per sq ft gap to V-Mart put at roughly INR135-140.

segments.name: LimeRoad / marketplace
segments.commentary: Marketplace loss reduced sharply YoY (management cites ~70% loss cut); business is CM3-profitable in high single digits. LimeRoad commission income fell 12%, which flows fully into gross margin.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex estimated at INR170-180 crore, mainly new stores, refurbishments and technology/AI spend; funded from internal accruals with no long-term debt.
Store expansion guidance unchanged at 13-15% area addition per year, net of 1-2% closures; 92 stores opened in FY26 with 12 closures.
Management says it aims for mid-single-digit or higher LTL growth and efficiency gains to lift margins; it did not commit to a timeline for returning to pre-COVID PAT margins of ~4-4.5%.
Rent-to-sales target of around 7% (6-7.5% range) for new stores.
ROCE ambition: currently ~14.5%, targeting 18%, then 20%+ over time.
capex_capacity: Q4 FY26 capex INR37 crore; FY26 capex INR159 crore, covering new stores, refurbishments and technology.
Capex per store about INR1.3-1.4 crore on a like-for-like basis; the higher blended figure reflects refurbishment spend, which runs on a 4-6 year cycle.
Gross new store additions were about 90 in FY26 (management corrected analyst figure of 75-78), with some larger-format stores.
Cost of capex may rise with raw material and group price inflation, though management says capex was negotiated lower in FY26.
Advance fabric booking: 50-60% of demand blocked until December.
demand_pricing: Management says consumption is healthy and footfalls are growing, mainly in Tier 2/3 towns; urban consumers held back spending during the geopolitical fear period.
Raw material inflation: yarn prices up 10-15%, translating to ~5-7% apparel cost increase; company absorbing 1-2% in some future deliveries and passing on a controlled amount.
Polyester is 70-75% of forward sourcing mix (75-80% in festive/winter, ~50% cotton in summer); 60-70% of apparel and non-apparel lines are poly-based.
Planned like-for-like price increase of 1-1.5% for similar products; ASP gains expected mainly from mix (for example, kurta sets).

Management views competitor store expansion as having limited impact on existing stores; sees a shift of customers from competitors to V-Mart. Notes over 60% of value retail spend still goes to unorganised retail.
Around 72% of sales come from repeat customers.

qa_highlights.question: How much raw material inflation is V-Mart facing, and how sensitive is the RM basket to crude?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a 10% rise in crude or yarn translates to about 5% in yarn cost and 1.5-2% in apparel cost for lower-priced products. Crude is up about 30-35%, which implies 3-4% higher garment cost for 100% polyester items; the company is offsetting this through fabric innovation and partly passing it on.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins expand about 120 bps in FY27 if LFL stays mid-single digit with no inflation shock?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not see major constraints and expects efficiency gains plus mid-single-digit or higher LFL to support margins; it flagged labour cost increases in Haryana and Noida as a risk. The CFO said conditions are not equal this year, so the outlook is uncertain.

qa_highlights.question: Will customers trade down, and what is the ASP trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said customers are not trading down. It expects a mix shift toward better products, with ASP balanced and no strong growth in entry-price products.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 capex INR170-180 crore when the analyst expected INR130-140 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the difference mainly goes to technology, with a heavier focus on AI-led initiatives, on top of new store and refurbishment capex.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk of a margin hiccup in festive and winter FY27 given advance booking and inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not expect a major margin jump or drop; the company has blocked 50-60% of needs until December and is focused on keeping value for loyal customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the medium-term ROC target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ROC is around 14.5% now, with a target of 18%, then 20%+ and possibly 22%.

risks_watch: Crude-linked yarn and polyester inflation (yarn +10-15%) may hit June-August deliveries and consumer sentiment; management says it may absorb some margin.
Vendor supply constraints from gas shortages, labour shortages and state elections in Bengal and Tamil Nadu, plus labour cost increases in Haryana and Noida.
Competitor store expansion and possible overlap with V-Mart's own store additions, which could weigh on SSSG after 10 quarters of growth.
Gross margin pressure from inventory provisioning and the fall in LimeRoad commission income (down 12%).
Real estate, construction and land costs rising, which could push rent-to-sales above the ~7% target.
Capex could rise due to inflation in group prices, against the INR170-180 crore plan.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on operations and growth, but cautious on the outlook. Management openly flags crude-driven inflation, yarn availability and consumer pressure as unresolved risks, and avoided committing to a timeline for margin recovery.
key_quotes: So quarter 4 has been a great growth quarter for us, with actually our highest ever quarterly new store additions as well as good like-to-like same-store sales growth, leading to a total sales growth of 24%.
We do not want to pass it on blindly. We do not want to pass it on like we did it in '22, '23.
So we will see good things coming in. But yes, we certainly have seen the impact of all these activities are getting nullified.

adds.what: Store area addition of 13-15% per year, net of 1-2% closures (92 stores opened in FY26, 12 closed)

growth.why: Management held store area addition guidance at 13-15% a year for FY27 with FY27 capex of INR170-180 crore for new stores, and reported 12% LTL growth and 24% sales growth in Q4; delivery is backed by store capex and footfall trends, but no order book or dated store pipeline was quantified, and it did not commit to a timeline for returning to pre-COVID PAT margins.
